header_summary:
Recent discussions in blockchain technology have highlighted the development of a recipe focusing on block-wide aggregation applications, first introduced in the Blockstream Research repository and notably mentioned in a Human Rights Foundation paper. The ongoing dialogue underscores the community's commitment to refining this concept, with plans to enhance its thoroughness based on further peer review and feedback. This process is a reflection of the broader collaborative nature of blockchain development, as indicated in the discussions [here](https://gnusha.org/pi/bitcoindev/Uk5a8rhAaNaCC8sif05lv1rmZLRYBCedbNVxPwDvHsWAA9Gbm36vGOw4XFvh7XG_MAJtiYBaD6BSEIr_KYWIxS5Ccm0OhwEIZo2gFeFfXvs=@protonmail.com/T/#m21a1bfa8b9667fa50af123bf759cf351c946d9bf).

The Blockchain Commons is scheduled to host a Gordian Developers Meeting focused on enhancing Bitcoin security through practical demonstrations and expert presentations by Shannon Appelcline and Stan Reeves. This event aims to foster a deeper understanding of Bitcoin’s security features, showcasing new techniques for secure data management and multisig setup exchange. Participants are encouraged to join via Zoom [here](https://us02web.zoom.us/j/88143195571?pwd=rgVeDCgOKT3IMtBiISego4p5wK0s6F.1), reflecting the event's emphasis on advancing Bitcoin security practices.

Furthermore, the `staletip` proposal aims to improve the observability of the stale rate within the Bitcoin network by allowing nodes to share information about stale tips, thus enhancing diagnostics and response times to network events. This initiative, leveraging collaborative efforts and technical innovations, seeks to provide better insights into block propagation dynamics and network health, with the community invited to review and provide feedback on the proposal and its proof-of-concept [here](https://github.com/pseudoramdom/bips/blob/staletip-bip-draft/bip-staletip.md).

The discourse on quantum readiness in Bitcoin highlights the urgency of integrating Post-Quantum Cryptography (PQC) proactively. Scott Aaronson's perspective encourages immediate action rather than waiting for quantum advancements, emphasizing a strategic approach to quantum computing akin to the controlled development of nuclear technologies. This discussion is part of a broader conversation on preparing digital infrastructures for future technological shifts, available for further reading [here](https://delvingbitcoin.org/t/pqc-output-type-discussion/2749/4).

recent_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Stale Tip Relay
recent_posts.summary: - The `staletip` proposal aims to improve Bitcoin network observability by tracking stale rates.  - It features P2P messaging for nodes to share data on stale tips, enhancing network diagnostics.  - Technical details include using BIP 434 messages and a cache system for managing stale tip data.

recent_posts.title: Onion Messaging DoS Threat Mitigations
recent_posts.summary:
- Implementing a hop-limit could enhance network efficiency by using high-capacity routes.
- Recent protocols integrate `option_onion_messages_only_channels`, altering node communication structures.
- Analyzing node support trends for `option_onion_messages` versus new changes is crucial for network insights.

recent_posts.title: PQC output type discussion

active_posts.title: BIP draft: CISA for Taproot Key Path Spends
active_posts.summary: - The new BIP draft introduces cross-input signature aggregation for Bitcoin transactions.  - Specifications for these aggregation schemes are detailed in BIP 458 and BIP 459.  - Community feedback is crucial for refining the proposal, with resources available for review.

active_posts.title: [BIP Proposal] Stale Tip Relay
active_posts.summary:
- The `staletip` proposal aims to improve Bitcoin network's stale rate observability.
- It includes a P2P system for nodes to communicate about stale block tips.
- The system restricts data sharing to recent and relevant network events.

active_posts.title: Bitcoin Resilience Presentations — August 5
active_posts.summary: - Blockchain Commons is hosting a Gordian Developers Meeting on August 5th.  - Shannon Appelcline and Stan Reeves will lead key presentations on Bitcoin security.  - The meeting will delve into advanced security techniques for Bitcoin Core.

active_posts.title: [BIP Draft] Segregated Data: a prunable, script-isolated block region for data carriage
active_posts.summary:
- SegData introduces efficient data storage in Bitcoin blocks while allowing optional data pruning.
- The proposal details technical modifications and new features to ensure data prunability and reduced costs.
- Open questions remain about implementation specifics, including transaction weight and privacy considerations.

active_posts.title: Onion Message Jamming in the Lightning Network
active_posts.summary:
- The Lightning Network's onion message forwarding faces rate-limiting and jamming vulnerabilities.
- Various implementations, including Core Lightning and Eclair, employ distinct rate-limiting methods against abuse.
- Proposed mitigation strategies range from upfront fees to backpropagation-based rate limiting.

active_posts.title: Transaction rate-limiting
active_posts.summary:
- Recent Bitcoin Core update optimizes transaction handling and CPU usage in nodes.
- Adjustments include a global queue system and new bandwidth rate limits.
- The update aims to enhance node robustness against high transaction volumes and network attacks.

today_in_history_posts.title: BIP Proposals for Output Script Descriptors
today_in_history_posts.summary:
- Andrew Chow proposed formalizing Output Script Descriptors through seven BIPs.
- The proposal includes descriptors for various Bitcoin scripts and seeks normalized software use.
- Some descriptors trace user-specific data like birth dates and gap limits for future wallets.

today_in_history_posts.title: Removing the Dust Limit
today_in_history_posts.summary:
- Jeremy Rubin proposes removing Bitcoin's dust limit for five reasons.
- He highlights potential uses for dust in smart contracts and privacy-preserving transactions.
- Rubin refutes spam concerns and suggests methods to prevent fingerprinting attacks.

today_in_history_posts.title: Sharing block templates
today_in_history_posts.summary:
- Recent changes in Bitcoin nodes include full replace-by-fee and enhanced spam filters.
- Compact block relay has significantly reduced Bitcoin's block propagation times.
- New strategies like weak blocks and template sharing improve network efficiency and privacy.
